name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia treaty limits since Feb
summary: Trump, Xi and Putin said on 19 Nov a nuclear war must never be fought, but set no arms-control talks or timetable
state: A joint declaration issued after the Trump–Xi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen on 19 Nov said there can be no winners in a nuclear war and committed to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks, but set no format, deadline or treaty (Gulf News, 20 Nov; Rappler). US–Russia treaty limits have been absent since New START expired in February. No nuclear test, alert-level change or threatened use was found as of 20 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: No change in day-to-day risk. The lapse of treaty limits mainly affects long-term stability between the largest nuclear powers.
rubric_hit: Watch: arms-control lapse without replacement (New START expired Feb; no successor agreed on 19 Nov)

sources.title: Gulf News — 'No winners in nuclear war': Trump, Xi, Putin pledge dialogue after Shenzhen summit
Rappler — Trump, Xi, Putin release 'peace declaration' from unprecedented summit

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
